key_insight: IMAGIN-4D shows that human-object interaction generation becomes much more controllable when the model is guided by a reference image, reducing ambiguity in grasp, pose, contact, and body-object layout. Instead of relying only on text or sparse trajectories, it uses visual reference to better match the intended interaction.
problem_solved: Existing HOI generation methods can follow the same prompt or object path but still produce many different interaction styles, making outputs inconsistent and hard to control. This paper tackles the ambiguity in interaction details that are not specified by text, object geometry, or waypoints alone.
method: Condition HOI generation on a reference image to disambiguate how the interaction should look.
Use the image guidance to control fine-grained interaction attributes such as grasp type, approach direction, body pose, object pose, and contact configuration.
Generate more precise and consistent human-object motion while preserving the intended action semantics and object trajectory.
impact: This is useful for practitioners building animation, robotics, AR/VR, and embodied AI systems that need realistic and user-controlled interaction generation. It improves reliability by giving models a stronger visual constraint than text-only or trajectory-only conditioning.
